concerns: Measurement feasibility: particle-count and immuno-capture sensitivity in low-biomass lavage/CSF is unvalidated and a single-point failure mode; spike-in recovery controls and buffer panels are required prior to in vivo work.

Process sensitivity: detergent/protease pre-treatment and capture-depletion workflows can non-specifically remove or denature non-EV components and alter downstream comparators, complicating interpretation and comparability.

Lot comparability: the candidate attribute (capture-positive, particle-co-localized, membrane-protected bioactivity) is high uncertainty and may vary by cell-bank, culture batch, and downstream fractionation; require reproducibility across ≥3 conditioned-medium lots before defining as a release test.

Stability: storage and handling (freeze–thaw, buffers, transport of low-biomass samples) may ablate membrane-protected signals; stability studies for the attribute in source and sampled matrices are needed.

Scale-up risk: even if rodent bridge is positive, NHP biodistribution suggests delivery efficiency may not scale — reliance on an intact-EV potency gate could force manufacturing/process changes that are difficult to scale or justify if translation to larger species fails.

Quality-attribute relevance: converting this mechanistic readout into a numeric release specification will require demonstration of quantitative correlation, assay robustness, and defined acceptance ranges; current proposal is qualitative and requires further analytical validation.
conclusion: The proposed in vivo→ex vivo bridge is a manufacturability- and CMC-relevant experiment and is justified by the available preclinical and consensus guidance, but it carries substantial measurement and scale-up risks that must be mitigated before execution. Specifically: (1) measurement feasibility for low-biomass nasal lavage/CSF is a critical gating risk (requires pre-validated capture reagents, buffer compatibility and spike-in recovery); (2) process sensitivity and comparability concerns arise from detergent/protease treatments and capture-depletion manipulations that can alter material composition beyond membrane disruption; (3) lot-to-lot consistency and stability of the proposed intact-EV attribute are unproven and will complicate release/specification strategy if the attribute is marginal or poorly reproducible; (4) cross-species delivery barriers (rodent signals vs. NHP negative biodistribution) create scale-up and translation risk such that a positive rodent bridge may not predict human-relevant manufacturable attributes. Recommend de-risking analytical sensitivity, defining tolerable process perturbations for comparators, and confirming reproducibility across ≥3 manufacturing lots before treating the intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected bioactivity as a release-linked quality attribute.
evidence_gap: No validated demonstration that the proposed immuno-capture + particle-count workflow has adequate sensitivity, specificity, and buffer compatibility for short-interval low-biomass nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples across production lots or larger species (NHP).
